chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad al-Katib from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:

I asked: A female slave and a free woman, a single house (estate) fell upon them, and they had given birth and died; how are they inherited? He said: A lot is cast for them three times as a group, so whichever of them the lot strikes inherits from the other.

key_terms.يُسْهَمُ: To cast lots / to draw lots

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a slave and a free woman who die simultaneously?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the mechanism of *al-khums* (one-fifth share) in simultaneous death (*al-khums*) for a slave and a free woman, a scenario where standard inheritance rules are ambiguous due to the uncertainty of who died first. By casting lots three times, the hadith establishes a probabilistic legal fiction where the 'winner' is deemed to have predeceased the other, thereby inheriting a portion of the other's estate before their own share is distributed. This method reflects the Shia juristic approach to resolving *gharar* (uncertainty) in inheritance cases involving mixed-status relatives, ensuring equitable distribution while acknowledging the distinct legal capacities of slaves and free persons.
